label: 02 / OUR MISSION
title: Students focus on their education, not on how to pay for it

cards.title: University-integrated, Sharia-guided support
cards.body: Overcome education-related financial barriers through an institutional, interest-free model.

cards.title: Proactive continuity
cards.body: Aim to support students throughout their education, as funding allows, resolving balances early before registration holds become crises.

cards.title: Protecting the student experience
cards.body: Tuition pressure should never cost a student their campus standing, academic momentum, or decades of compound debt.

note: Early-stage thesis: institutional integration stops financial dropouts before registration holds trigger.

label: 03 / STUDENT EXPERIENCES
title: Financial pressure can shape a student's whole path
subtitle: Four anonymized profiles based on real experiences of New Jersey students from 2019 to 2025.

cards.title: One Semester Away from Graduation
cards.body: Final-semester tuition remained uncovered despite work and federal loans. Late fees delayed the diploma; the unpaid balance later went to collections.

cards.title: A Dream of Medicine. A Conflict of Conviction.
cards.body: Accepted to medical school without family support, this student faces high costs and interest-bearing loans that conflict with their faith.

cards.title: A Family That Can Afford College — Just Not All at Once
cards.body: Several siblings pursue college together, but upfront balances and short payment schedules make affordability and school choice difficult.

cards.title: Working to Stay in School
cards.body: Working to cover tuition and living costs leaves less time for academics; when income falls short, a student may stop out.

note: These stories do not establish Junnah eligibility. A future program would require students to apply for all available eligible non-interest-bearing aid first and would consider only remaining verified eligible tuition gaps, subject to funding and review.

label: 04 / MARKET GAP & EXISTING DEMAND
title: Demand exists. Funding is the bottleneck.
subtitle: Students already seek interest-free education support, but existing funding sources may not meet every eligible student's need.

cards.title: Established demand
cards.body: Students already turn to Muslim financial institutions and charitable organizations for interest-free education funding.

cards.title: Limited capital
cards.body: Community funding pools and charitable programs may be unable to meet the needs of every eligible student.

cards.title: The gap Junnah addresses
cards.body: Junnah partners directly with universities to fund tuition upfront, giving students an interest-free repayment option while helping institutions receive tuition payments earlier.

note: Junnah is an early-stage concept. University partnerships, funding capacity, and the scale of unmet need remain to be validated.

label: 05 / SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
title: Junnah is workflow infrastructure, not a chatbot or a loan marketplace
subtitle: An aid-first workflow verifies the eligible tuition gap before any proposed financing.

cards.title: Student submits a tuition-gap request
cards.body: For a new term, shares school, amount, deadline, and available aid or aid-application information.

cards.title: Verify aid and remaining gap
cards.body: University confirms all available eligible aid was applied and verifies charges, balance, and deadline.

cards.title: Review the case
cards.body: A human reviewer assesses the remaining gap and circumstances.

cards.title: Agree clear terms
cards.body: Student reviews and accepts documented, principal-only terms.

cards.title: Pay the university
cards.body: Only if approved and funding is available.

cards.title: Track and get support
cards.body: Student follows principal, repayment, and hardship options.

label: 06 / CIRCUMSTANTIAL UNDERWRITING
title: Same balance, very different students
subtitle: Three illustrative student profiles demonstrating why human review looks at real capacity rather than automated credit scores.

cards.title: Profile A · Employed, with family
cards.body: Earns part-time wages, but income is absorbed by essential household contributions. Living at home does not mean tuition liquidity exists.
cards.note: Review insight: family co-residence does not equal tuition surplus.

cards.title: Profile B · Employed, independent
cards.body: Maintains consistent employment but carries full rent, utilities, food, and transit obligations. Zero discretionary margin remains for lump-sum term fees.
cards.note: Review insight: high fixed living overheads exhaust earnings.

cards.title: Profile C · Unemployed, with family
cards.body: Zero earned income. Case management reviews household capacity and employment horizon rather than dismissing the student for lacking current payroll.
cards.note: Review insight: requires assessing actual household support capacity.

note: Fictional profiles for review design. No standard automated algorithm captures non-discretionary family support obligations.

label: 07 / STUDENT TRUST & GOVERNANCE
title: Fair review and principal-only repayment build student trust

cards.title: 01 · Human accountability
cards.body: No standard credit-score test; human reviewers stay accountable, with documented reasons and an appeal route.

cards.title: 02 · Qard Hasan structure
cards.body: Students repay principal only; $4,000 at $100 a month is 40 months, illustrative.

cards.title: 03 · Structured hardship support
cards.body: Deferment, reduced payments, periodic review.

cards.title: 04 · Proposed administration fee
cards.body: Illustratively $25 per new contract, charged only if approved, never at submission and never added to principal; pending legal and Sharia review, not an approved term.

label: 08 / COMMERCIAL ARCHITECTURE
title: Universities pay for software; investors share eligible company profit

cards.title: Enterprise SaaS hypotheses · University revenue models
cards.body: Institutions preserve retention by clearing administrative drops. Testing software subscriptions, onboarding implementation fees, administrative servicing fees, or volume tiers.
cards.note: Unvalidated hypothesis: pricing models require pilot discovery.

cards.title: Ethical investor return · Contractual profit participation
cards.body: Investors hold rights strictly to eligible operating company profits. Investor returns never touch philanthropic donations or student principal repayments.
cards.note: Returns are commercial, unguaranteed, and ring-fenced from student repayments.

note: University willingness to pay and exact SaaS contract amounts remain unvalidated hypotheses for pilot testing.

label: 09 / SCALABLE UNIVERSITY MODEL
title: More university partners. More recurring revenue. Greater impact.
subtitle: Junnah connects university tuition payments, student financing, and institutional revenue in one proposed platform.

flow.title: Tuition paid upfront
flow.body: Remaining eligible gap after aid, subject to approval and funding

flow.title: Capital revolves
flow.body: Principal repayments may replenish the pool

revenueStreams.title: Recurring SaaS fees
revenueStreams.body: University payments for ongoing platform access.

revenueStreams.title: Per-student service fees
revenueStreams.body: Institutional revenue that can grow with students served.

revenueStreams.title: Student administration fees
revenueStreams.body: Proposed one-time agreement-administration fee to cover administration, not investor returns; subject to validation and review.

chart.definitions: U = university partners · N = students served annually

fundingNote: Early on, Junnah may not be able to cover each student's full eligible balance. As revenue and financing capacity grow, our goal is to support students throughout their education, subject to available funds, approval, and university participation.
takeaway: A growing university network can expand recurring institutional revenue while a revolving financing pool helps fund successive student cohorts.
note: Illustrative scenarios, not projections. Revenue is not profit or investor return; university revenue and pool capital are separate. Outcomes depend on adoption, repayment, available funding, costs, and final agreements. Student fees are excluded.

label: 10 / HOW UNIVERSITIES BENEFIT
title: Universities gain a structured path for unresolved balances

cards.title: Retention and re-enrollment
cards.body: A defined pathway for students blocked by balances. Effect on retention is to be measured with predicted higher retention and graduation rates.

cards.title: Administrative efficiency
cards.body: One place for intake, verification, review, status and reporting across departments.

cards.title: Balance resolution
cards.body: The separate pool may address a verified eligible tuition gap after available eligible non-interest-bearing aid is applied, subject to approval and funds.

cards.title: Reporting and accountability
cards.body: Applications, decisions, amounts disbursed and processing times.

cards.title: Preventing collections at source
cards.body: Upfront tuition payment can address eligible balances before they enter collections and may reduce collection risk for supported cases.

note: Pricing and value are unvalidated and must be tested with each institution. Junnah will not eliminate collections in every case. The university pays for software and administration only, separate from charitable funds and student repayments.

label: 11 / WHAT JUNNAH IS — AND ISN'T
title: Not Charity. Not Interest-Bearing Debt. A Different Model.
subtitle: It is a proposed revolving student-financing fund: principal repayments may support future students, while university revenue is intended to fund operations. Philanthropic contributions may supplement the pool; long-term self-sustainability remains unproven.

cards.title: Vault I · Revolving Student-Financing Pool
cards.body: May include philanthropic contributions and other permitted capital. Pays approved eligible tuition balances upfront; students repay principal under agreed terms.
cards.note: Repayments may be recycled for future students. Defaults, hardship relief, and fund restrictions can reduce available capital.

cards.title: Vault II · Operating Equity / Investor Capital
cards.body: Funds software engineering, compliance, operations, and team payroll. Any investment in the student-financing pool would be separately structured and governed.
cards.note: Investors accept genuine business risk for a share of actual profits, not a fixed return. Student principal repayments remain separate from company revenue.

cards.title: Vault III · Earned Revenue / University Contracts
cards.body: Commercial software licenses and institutional servicing fees paid by university partners for workflow infrastructure and retention management.
cards.note: Intended operating revenue for the management company; commercial viability still needs validation.

note: Proposed structure; legal, regulatory, accounting, and qualified Sharia review required. A revolving model does not guarantee the fund or company will become self-sustaining.

label: 12 / PROPOSED CAPITAL FRAMEWORK
title: Match each dollar to its purpose and time horizon
subtitle: A proposed framework separates near-term liquidity needs from capital that may be invested over longer periods.

cards.title: Bucket 1 · Tuition liquidity
cards.body: Funds for imminent university payments, expected withdrawals, and short-term repayment gaps. Prioritize capital preservation and ready access—not investment returns.
cards.note: Liquidity comes first for scheduled obligations and near-term needs.

cards.title: Bucket 2 · Capital preservation
cards.body: Funds not needed immediately could be considered for appropriately screened, relatively low-risk, liquid assets aligned with Sharia principles, subject to qualified review.
cards.note: Lower risk is not no risk; asset values, access, and returns are not guaranteed.

cards.title: Bucket 3 · Long-term growth
cards.body: Only genuine surplus with a sufficiently long time horizon could be considered for diversified growth investments after near-term obligations and reserves are covered.
cards.note: Greater potential upside also means potential losses and prolonged underperformance.

note: Concept only—not an approved investment policy or investment advice. Invest only funds whose terms permit it; student principal and restricted gifts remain separately governed. Any allocation requires cash-flow, legal/fiduciary, custody, governance, and qualified Sharia review. Values, returns, and liquidity are not guaranteed.

label: 13 / CASH-FLOW STRESS TEST
title: Can the pool meet next semester's commitments if repayments are late?
subtitle: Example model template · Opening pool + repayments received − tuition disbursed − other outflows = cash available for the next term.

cards.title: Opening available pool
cards.body: Set the initial pool size using liquid capital available for student support after restrictions and protected reserves.

cards.title: Tuition commitments
cards.body: Multiply the average eligible gap per student after aid by the number funded, and map each university payment due date.

cards.title: Repayment schedule
cards.body: Map principal due by student and date. Count repayments as cash only when received.

cards.title: Defaults and delays
cards.body: Reduce expected inflows for realistic defaults and recovery; shift receipt dates in late-payment cases.

cards.title: Next-semester coverage test
cards.body: At every due date, test whether cash on hand can meet committed eligible tuition payments if repayments arrive late.

note: Run base and downside cases, including late/no repayments and higher defaults. This is a model template, not a forecast; pool size, student count, funding gaps, repayment terms, and loss assumptions still need validation.

label: 14 / PILOT SPECIFICATION
title: A one-semester pilot with about 10 students tests the real workflow

cards.title: Scope
cards.body: One New Jersey university, about 10 students, one semester.

cards.title: Long-term vision
cards.body: Support from a student's first semester through graduation; the pilot starts narrow.

cards.title: Pilot pathways
cards.body: Final-semester shortfall, registration barrier, graduation-clearance barrier; rent and living costs excluded.

cards.title: Measures
cards.body: Time to decision, amounts disbursed, barrier resolved, cost per case, hardship, university willingness to renew, retention rate, graduation rate.

cards.title: Illustrative budget
cards.body: Dependent on university tuition, software/administration costs, and number of students in pilot.

cards.title: Aid-first requirement
cards.body: Students must apply for all available eligible non-interest-bearing aid; the pilot assesses only the verified eligible tuition gap remaining afterward.

label: 15 / THE JUNNAH ECOSYSTEM
title: One coordinated experience across the support model

label: 16 / STAGE & PARTNERSHIP ASK
title: Where we are, and what we want from a partner

cards.title: Where we stand
cards.body: Built from lived experience. Solo software-engineer founder at pre-validation concept stage. Zero institutional partners, formal funding, or commercial revenue yet.

cards.title: What must be validated
cards.body: Legal structure, formal Sharia advisory certification, and university willingness to pay software fees.

cards.title: What we seek from partners
cards.body: Model stress-testing, introductions to New Jersey higher education leadership, pilot advisory support, and early hiring alignment.
